fatal_errors: The proposed DSC–dilatometry protocol does not reconstruct the target DFT/MTP/FEP approach or address its central objective of efficiently predicting liquid-phase free energies across alloy compositions.

The cited evidence supports DSC heat-capacity measurements up to the solidus, but does not establish simultaneous dilatometric measurement of liquid volume, fusion enthalpy, or the claimed ±1–2% and ±5% accuracies.

Ordinary solid-sample dilatometry cannot straightforwardly measure equilibrium liquid volume after loss of specimen shape and containment; no high-temperature liquid-density or container-interaction method is specified.

The entropy-of-fusion rationale is inaccurate: at equilibrium it is primarily obtained as ΔH_fus/T_m, whereas heat-capacity baseline subtraction concerns additional temperature-dependent entropy contributions.
The hypothesis omits the requested liquid-phase thermodynamic properties beyond an asserted volume change and provides no route to liquid free energy, heat capacity, or related quantities.

The selected conventional HEAs and experimental conditions do not match the disordered BCC TaVCrW refractory alloy, 0 GPa calculations, 2000–2400 K range, exchange-correlation treatments, or target computational benchmarks.
explanation: The response recognizes several requested observables and proposes a cross-validated experiment, so it has limited problem-level alignment and some discriminability. However, it is scientifically and evidentially disconnected from the target: the intended advance is replacing EAM/TI with a high-fidelity MTP/FEP free-energy workflow, including electronic and short-range-order corrections. None of the target quantitative results—sub-meV/atom agreement, approximately 80% savings or 20× acceleration, electronic 48–57 K shifts, or 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization—are recovered. The cited paper only substantiates DSC heat-capacity measurements up to the solidus and cannot support the proposed fusion and liquid-volume performance. Consequently, this is not a sufficiently supported alternative for determining the full requested property set across the HEA family.
